issue.title: Diagnose the race between agents-sync publication and workspace-prep clean/reset against the shared agents sidecar clone
issue.description: Root-cause the race that emptied the sase agents-repo owner manifest from 1389 hoods to 1 hood in a single publication: agents-repo commit 5f244a229 (2026-08-06 09:11:53, 1389 hoods) -> 6ad0b6e2a (2026-08-06 09:16:12, 1 hood, 'tv' only), with the commit's diff losing the manifest entries plus 1390 lines of the browsing README. 6ad0b6e2a is the exact fetched_sha recorded in five stale incoming-cache items that misclassified this machine's own 24 legacy-v1 runs as an unknown-user import (surfaced as a green unknown-user badge in ACE). The agents-repo reflog shows a whole-tree 'reset: moving to HEAD' + 'checkout: moving from main to main' one second before that commit (2026-08-06 09:16:11) -- the signature of vcs_clean_workspace (git reset --hard HEAD + git clean -fd) followed by a branch checkout, i.e. a workspace-preparation pass running against the agents sidecar clone at ~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/repos/agents, which all 24 sase_<N> workspaces share. The 1391 hood directories under users/bbugyi200/machines/athena/hoods/ survived intact -- only the manifest.json that references them was truncated, meaning publication_planning.plan_hoods's read_owner_manifest() must have seen a missing or freshly-reset manifest.json (v2_manifest_io.read_owner_manifest returns an empty V2OwnerManifest when the file is not present) and then republished from that empty base for a single targeted hood ('tv'), overwriting the real manifest. The precise interleaving that made the file unreadable at that instant -- whether the clean/reset briefly deleted manifest.json while a concurrent publish read it, or checkout raced a write, or something else entirely -- is not diagnosed. Discovered and surfaced via plan sase/repos/plans/202608/unknown_user_legacy_hood_ownership.md, whose Fix 3/Fix 4 (landed in that plan's implementation) harden publication_planning.plan_hoods to raise AgentsSyncFormatError instead of silently republishing from an empty manifest when on-disk hood directories exist, and add a 'sase agent sync --repair-manifest' command to reconstruct lost manifest entries from intact on-disk snapshots -- but those are containment/repair, not a fix for the underlying race. A related precedent exists: sase-ab.1 (closed) solved an analogous problem for the *beads* sidecar, teaching workspace-preparation to protect or publish local-only bead-store commits before a clean+hard checkout discards them; that fix's shape (protect-before-clean) may be a useful starting point but does not itself cover the agents sidecar's manifest.json, since sase-ab.1 was scoped to bead-store commit protection only. Scope: reproduce or trace the concurrent-workspace-preparation-vs-agents-sync-publication interleaving against the shared agents sidecar clone, and land whichever fix shape avoids the corruption at its source (e.g. per-workspace clones instead of a shared one, a lock that workspace-prep's clean/reset respects, or protecting/publishing local-only agents-sidecar commits before a hard reset the way sase-ab.1 did for beads).

payload.entry:
Root-caused the manifest collapse to an uncoordinated workspace-preparation pass over the machine-shared agents sidecar clone, and landed a lock fix at the source.

DIAGNOSIS. The actor is 'sase repo open agents'. repo_handler_open -> workspace_handler_list.prepare_opened_checkout -> axe.runner_workspace.prepare_workspace runs run_sase_hg_clean (vcs_clean_workspace = git reset --hard HEAD + git clean -fd) then provider.checkout(default parent) against the resolved checkout. For the agents sidecar that checkout is ~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/repos/agents -- one clone shared by all 24 workspaces (confirmed 'agents sidecar 24/24' in sase repo list), unlike the per-workspace sidecars under sase/repos/. Confirmed on the live clone: reflog has 'reset: moving to HEAD' + 'checkout: moving from main to main' at 2026-08-06 09:16:11, one second before the truncating commit 6ad0b6e2a at 09:16:12; a second bare 'checkout: moving from main to main' at 09:19:44 pairs with the repo-open audit record (sase repo log --repo agents: last_opened_at 2026-08-06T13:19:45Z, agent u0, workspace #11) -- 47 opens by 44 distinct agents against that one clone.

THE INTERLEAVING. Every agents-sync mutator serializes on <git_dir>/sase-agents-sync.lock (git_sync._sync_project, commit_publication, incoming_integration, publication_repair, v1_retirement, status, commit_finalizer_git). prepare_workspace was the one actor that took no lock. agents-sync stages its whole regenerated payload in the worktree before commit_agents_payload_if_dirty commits it, so at that instant manifest.json was dirty-tracked. git reset --hard rewrites a dirty tracked file by unlinking it before recreating it; v2_manifest_io.read_owner_manifest returns an empty V2OwnerManifest for a non-existent path, and publication_planning.plan_hoods seeds its entry map from that read. A targeted single-hood publication ('tv') that read inside the unlink window therefore republished from an empty base, emitting the 1-hood manifest while all 1391 hood directories stayed on disk. git clean -fd compounds this by deleting untracked staged payload.

FIX. src/sase/axe/runner_workspace.py: prepare_workspace now runs its clean/checkout/sync pass (extracted to _prepare_workspace_locked) inside _agents_sidecar_sync_guard, which takes the same sase-agents-sync.lock when _agents_sidecar_clone_root identifies the target as the machine-shared <sase_projects_dir>/<key>/repos/agents clone, and returns False with a named diagnostic when the lock is busy. Every other workspace, including a workspace-scoped sase/repos/agents clone, is unaffected. This is the sase-ab.1 protect-before-clean shape applied to the agents sidecar; no commits are at risk here (reset --hard HEAD drops none and payload is regenerated every pass), so a lock is sufficient and no rescue ref is needed.

TESTS. New tests/test_axe_runner_workspace_agents_lock.py: a busy sync lock blocks the clean entirely (run_sase_hg_clean not called, returns False); the lock is provably held across the clean and released afterward; a workspace-scoped agents clone stays unguarded. Verified red before the fix (2 of 3 fail) and green after.

VERIFIED. just install; just check -- all lint gates green (fmt, ruff, mypy, pyscripts, symvision, toobig, SASE validation, committed plans) and 25968 passed / 1 failed. The single failure, tests/test_plan_display.py::test_malformed_header_block_leaves_authored_metadata_visible, reproduces on a clean stashed tree, is unrelated to this change, and is already fixed on origin/master by d9c13549f (sase-g4.3), which rewrites that exact fixture to assert validation_ok is False; this workspace checkout (9a366e0d6, 10:00) predates it while carrying the newer sase-core-rs wheel. No task bead filed for it.

SCOPE NOTE. The plan's Fix 3 (plan_hoods raising instead of republishing from an empty manifest) and Fix 4 (sase agent sync --repair-manifest) are not on master yet and are deliberately untouched here -- they are that plan's containment/repair work, this bead is the source fix.
